title: PathWise: Planning through World Model for Automated Heuristic Design via Self-Evolving LLMs
one_liner: Search for stronger optimization heuristics by keeping a running record of past design choices and planning the next change from that record.
lead: This paper studies automated heuristic design for combinatorial optimization. Earlier systems often try one prompt after another with fixed mutation rules, so they repeat weak ideas and forget why earlier attempts failed. PathWise turns heuristic design into a step-by-step planning problem, where several agents share a structured record of the search so that each new candidate is chosen with awareness of what already happened.

problem.h2: Why automatic heuristic search wastes effort
paras: A heuristic for a hard search problem is usually built by many small design choices. One change may alter how states are scored, another may alter how branches are explored, and another may change which candidate solution is kept. If an automated system does not remember those choices clearly, it can circle back to the same dead end.

That waste matters because evaluating a heuristic can be expensive. A search loop that keeps proposing related weak ideas burns time on repeated tests instead of moving toward a better design. The paper asks how to make the search stateful so that each new proposal uses earlier evidence.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Store the search history in an entailment graph, let one agent plan the next design action, let another agent generate the candidate heuristic, and let critic agents summarize what the search has learned so far.

panels.title: 1. Start with a hard optimization task
panels.viz_args: The system must invent a useful heuristic
panels.caption: The goal is not to solve one instance once. The goal is to discover a reusable rule set.

panels.title: 2. Early attempts pile up
panels.viz_args: Many candidate heuristics are tried and scored
panels.caption: A plain loop can forget which changes helped and which ones failed.

panels.title: 3. Build a search record
panels.caption: The record keeps the branching history visible so that the next choice can use it.

panels.title: 4. Plan the next action from that record
panels.viz_args: A policy agent chooses how the next heuristic should differ
panels.caption: The system acts more deliberately because the next step is chosen from known search context.

panels.title: 5. The search improves over time
panels.caption: The loop converges faster because it reuses earlier lessons instead of restarting from vague memory.

steps.text: Write earlier heuristic proposals, edits, and outcomes into an entailment graph so that the system has a compact record of the search.
A policy agent decides whether to refine, combine, or redirect current ideas because different search states call for different next moves.
A world model agent produces a candidate heuristic that follows the chosen action.
Critic agents summarize what worked or failed so that later rounds inherit the lesson.
The new outcome is added back into the search record so that future proposals can avoid redundant branches.

paras: The paper changes heuristic design from a loose cycle of prompt variation into an explicit sequential decision process. The important shift is that the search state is written down and reused at every round.
object.object: the next design action taken during heuristic search

hidden.name: which branch of the design search is worth pursuing next
paras: The key hidden quantity is not the score of the current heuristic alone. It is the future value of the next branch choice. A branch that looks modest now may open a useful direction, while a branch with a decent short-term score may only repeat old ideas.

PathWise tries to estimate that hidden value from the search record. The shared graph matters because it records what was tried, what failed, and what remains plausible, so the planner can choose the next move with more context.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark decisions where remembering the search history can change the next move the most.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is which next change is most worth testing after everything the system has already learned.
The method uses a stateful search record so that planning over heuristic evolution becomes a history-aware decision problem instead of a memoryless mutation loop.

mechanism.h2: Why this works: keep the search state and plan from it
paras: A fixed-rule search loop often stalls because it treats each round almost independently. Even if it stores old candidates, it may not convert that archive into a decision about what to try next. PathWise does more than save history. It organizes history into a form that later agents can read and act on.

That helps because the policy agent can choose a better next action when it sees earlier failures, partial successes, and promising combinations. The critic summaries also matter because they turn scattered trial results into reusable guidance. The result is faster convergence by reducing redundant evaluations and by steering the search toward branches that have supporting evidence.

stages.s: Optimization task plus earlier search history
Write history into a structured graph
Plan the next heuristic edit from that graph
Generate, test, and critique the candidate
A stronger heuristic search loop because each round uses earlier evidence

math.h2: Choose the branch with the best expected future payoff
math.words: A simple summary is to score each possible next action by combining the quality of the resulting heuristic and the information already stored about that branch. The planner prefers the action with the largest expected value.
symbols: overall value of choosing one next design action
how good the resulting heuristic is expected to be
how strongly the stored search history supports that action
weight on the history-based part of the score

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Action A repeats a mutation that was already weak in two earlier rounds.
Its expected heuristic value is 5 and its history value is 0, so with rho = 1 its total score is 5.
Action B combines two partial ideas that earlier critics marked as promising.
Its expected heuristic value is 5 and its history value is 3, so its total score is 8.
The planner picks Action B because the search record says that branch has better future promise.

math.note: The paper uses a richer multi-agent system, but this equation captures the core point that past search evidence should affect the next design step.

charts.title: Fixed-rule automated design
charts.note: A static loop wastes work because it re-explores similar weak ideas and carries little useful memory across rounds.

charts.title: PathWise
charts.note: The paper reports stronger search behavior because state-aware planning helps the system spend more trials on branches with better support.

items.b: The search record can become biased.
items.html: If early critic judgments are poor, later planning may keep favoring the wrong branches because the stored history keeps repeating that mistake.
A cluttered record may make branch choice worse because important lessons can be buried under many weak notes.

items.b: Planning may overcommit to local improvements.
items.html: A system that trusts recent progress too much can miss a larger redesign because it keeps refining the current branch.
The framework is useful because it gives heuristic search a memory that directly shapes future actions.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small automated heuristic-design loop for one combinatorial optimization task, such as vehicle routing or job scheduling. Compare a plain mutation loop against a PathWise-style loop that stores branch history, chooses the next action from that history, and writes critic summaries after each trial.

The demo should track best heuristic score over time, number of repeated weak branches, and number of evaluations needed to reach a target quality. The PathWise-style loop should reach that target sooner because its planner reuses earlier search evidence instead of revisiting the same failed direction.
demo.metric_eq: search_gain = evaluations_baseline - evaluations_pathwise ; repeat_drop = repeated_branches_baseline - repeated_branches_pathwise
demo.closing: The result should show that search memory changes what the system tries next, and that this change improves heuristic discovery because earlier failures and partial successes remain available when the planner chooses the next branch.
